displayQuote: Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past are certain to miss the future

meta.title: Who really said "Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past are certain to miss the future"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes — John F. Kennedy said it, in his June 25, 1963 speech at the Paulskirche in Frankfurt. The popular version drops his words “or the present.”
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past are certain to miss the future'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Kennedy: from his June 25, 1963 Frankfurt address. The widely shared version quietly drops “or the present.”

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: Kennedy delivered these words in his “Address in the Assembly Hall at the Paulskirche in Frankfurt” on June 25, 1963. The line is confirmed in the official transcript — though he actually said “those who look only to the past or the present,” a phrase the popular version drops.

docMeta.dd: Address in the Assembly Hall at the Paulskirche in Frankfurt

source.excerpt: For time and the world do not stand still. Change is the law of life. And those who look only to the past or the present are certain to miss the future.
trail: The primary transcript appears in the American Presidency Project’s copy of the Public Papers of the Presidents ↗, dated June 25, 1963.
Quotation trackers such as WIST ↗ cite the same Paulskirche address and preserve the full wording — “past or the present.”
Most viral copies (e.g. BrainyQuote ↗) trim the line to “look only to the past,” losing Kennedy’s original “or the present.”
source.cutTag: ↑ the popular version drops “or the present”
source.excerptNote: Kennedy reaches this line moments after invoking Goethe’s Faust — warning that liberty is endangered “if we pause for the passing moment, if we rest on our achievements, if we resist the pace of progress.”

author.name: John F. Kennedy
author.heading: About John F. Kennedy
author.bio: John Fitzgerald Kennedy (1917–1963) served as the 35th President of the United States from 1961 until his assassination in November 1963. A gifted orator, his June 1963 European tour produced several of his most quoted lines — most famously “Ich bin ein Berliner,” delivered in Berlin the day after this Frankfurt address. The Paulskirche speech, given in a hall symbolic of German democracy, framed change and progress as the condition of a free society.

misattribution.heading: The misquotation
misattribution.intro: The attribution to Kennedy is correct — but the wording usually is not. The line is almost always shortened.

items.who: “…those who look only to the past are certain to miss the future”
items.why: Kennedy actually said “those who look only to the past or the present,” per the official transcript ↗. Popular copies drop the middle phrase.

misattribution.truthLine: The words are genuinely Kennedy’s, from his June 25, 1963 Frankfurt address ↗ — just usually quoted with “or the present” missing.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Speaking in the Paulskirche — the seat of Germany’s first freely elected parliament in 1848 — Kennedy used the setting to argue that free societies stay free only by embracing progress. The “change is the law of life” passage is his answer to Goethe’s Faust, who forfeited his soul by begging the passing moment to stay.
detailsBody: The Frankfurt speech came during a landmark European trip: two days before, Kennedy had spoken in Cologne, and the day after — June 26, 1963 — he delivered the “Ich bin ein Berliner” address in West Berlin.
context.pull: For time and the world do not stand still.
